name: MMM Beauty
seen: The logo is a gold and deep-green serif MM with the word BEAUTY under it.
The site is light: cool off-white and white, with cream at the top. The cookie bar is dark green. It is not a black site.

The first screen is a full-width looping video: a blurred pink-brown close-up too soft to say what it shows, with the headline over it in thin letter-spaced serif, an italic line, and a mint-green Book Now button.
Buttons are mint-green gradient pills; cards have thin dark outlines and rounded corners; section headings have a short mint bar beside them.
The three service cards use bright, generic-looking photos (hands, a face with eyes closed, a facial). The package cards use flat-lay props and a Dermalogica product shot.
The About page has a real photo of Meghan working on a client, with pills: VTCT certified, Brackley since 2023, Over 300 clients.

The Gallery shows real nail and brow close-ups. In the screens looked at, the nails sit on light grey, white or skin tones; some have a dark sleeve or dark fabric behind the hand, but none is a black studio setup. Most of the nail set is Christmas themed (snowflakes, reds) though the capture was in late September. The filter offers Nails and Brows only.
Treatments lists services with photos and a Most Popular badge on Builder Gel Manicure. Booking leaves the site for a Square page, which has Square's own look and a Square cookie prompt.
check: Only gallery screens 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and 8 of 8 were looked at; screens 4 and 6 were not.
The Most Popular badge needs booking evidence. The earlier claim that soft-square is the most-booked nail shape is still unsupported.
The service-card photos look like stock images. Their source is not known.
The exact disputed picture from the earlier review is still not identified.
Small boxed characters appear before Nails and Brows in the gallery filter. They may be missing symbols in the capture browser.
The cookie bar was left open.
